column5: Curate and develop resources on applying systems thinking to sustainability challenges. Coordinate with SE practitioners to create case studies, tools, and guidelines. Facilitate discussions linking system dynamics models to sustainability outcomes.

column4: A methodology to evaluate the environmental impacts of a product, process, or system across its entire life cycle — from raw material extraction through end-of-life disposal.

column4: Systematic review and synthesis of academic and industry publications relevant to sustainability in systems engineering.
column5: Define scope and search strategy. Gather, screen, and synthesise relevant papers and reports. Maintain an annotated bibliography and produce summary documents to inform other WG workstreams.

column4: Exploring how sustainable business models (e.g. circular economy, product-as-a-service) intersect with and influence systems engineering practice.
column5: Research and document sustainable business model archetypes. Develop guidance on how SE teams can support and enable sustainable business strategies. Produce case studies and frameworks for practitioners.

column4: Leveraging digital engineering approaches — including MBSE, digital twins, and simulation — to design, analyse, and optimise systems for sustainability.
column5: Identify how digital engineering tools can quantify and improve sustainability metrics. Develop reference models, integration patterns, and worked examples. Coordinate with tool vendors and standards bodies where applicable.

column4: Methods and guidance for eliciting, specifying, verifying, and validating sustainability-related requirements within SE processes.
column5: Create templates and taxonomies for sustainability requirements (environmental, social, economic). Map them to existing SE requirement frameworks and standards. Produce guidance documents and example requirement sets.

column4: Managing and moderating the WG's presence on INCOSE Connect — the INCOSE member community platform — to foster engagement and knowledge sharing.
column5: Monitor and respond to posts on the WG's INCOSE Connect space. Curate and publish content updates, announce events, and ensure discussions remain productive. Onboard new members and maintain community guidelines.

column4: Planning and delivering a series of webinars presenting research, practice, and dialogue on sustainability topics relevant to the INCOSE community.
column5: Identify and recruit speakers, define a forward schedule, and coordinate logistics. Manage promotion, registration, and post-event materials (recordings, summaries). Gather attendee feedback to improve future sessions.

column4: Contributing sustainability content to the Systems Engineering Body of Knowledge — the authoritative online reference for SE knowledge.
column5: Identify gaps in existing SEBoK content related to sustainability. Draft and submit new or revised articles following SEBoK editorial guidelines. Coordinate reviews with WG members and SEBoK editors until acceptance.

column4: Building and maintaining relationships with external organisations, sister working groups, standards bodies, and industry partners relevant to sustainability in SE.
column5: Map key external stakeholders and organisations. Identify relevant forums and events and make sure the WG is represented there. Facilitate introductions and collaborations. Maintain a contact list and provide regular updates to the WG on partnership opportunities.

column4: Researching and documenting the sustainability challenges, priorities, and requirements of organisations and practitioners across different industry sectors.
column5: Design and conduct surveys, interviews, or workshops with industrial stakeholders. Analyse and synthesise findings into reports or personas. Use insights to inform the WG's priorities and ensure outputs are relevant to practitioners.

column4: Managing the Sustainability Working Group's GitHub presence — including repositories, file organisation, and access — to ensure WG outputs and resources are version-controlled, accessible, and well-maintained
column5: Set up and maintain repositories for WG deliverables (documents, models, templates). Establish contribution guidelines and a consistent file structure. Manage member access and permissions. Review and merge pull requests, and keep the repository up to date with the latest WG outputs.

column4: Applying enterprise architecture frameworks (e.g. UAF, TOGAF, DoDAF) to understand and represent how sustainability considerations are embedded across an organisation's strategy, processes, systems, and technology.
column5: Develop guidance on integrating sustainability into enterprise architecture models and views. Produce reference architectures and worked examples. Connect findings to other WG workstreams such as Business Models and Digital Engineering.

column4: Identifying and developing the systems, tools, and infrastructure that enable sustainable practices within systems engineering — such as measurement frameworks, decision-support tools, and sustainability assessment platforms.
column5: Map the enabling systems needed to support the WG's sustainability agenda. Develop or curate tools and frameworks that practitioners can apply. Document requirements and use cases, and coordinate with relevant WG workstreams to ensure alignment.

column4: Exploring regenerative approaches in systems engineering — going beyond sustainability to design systems that actively restore and replenish natural, social, and economic resources rather than merely reducing harm.
column5: Research and synthesise emerging thinking on regenerative design and engineering. Develop guidance on how SE practitioners can apply regenerative principles. Produce case studies and contribute findings to SEBoK and other WG outputs.

column4: Examining how circular economy principles — such as designing for longevity, reuse, remanufacturing, and closed-loop material flows — can be applied within systems engineering practice.
column5: Research circular economy frameworks and their relevance to SE. Develop practical guidance and tools for integrating circularity into system design and life cycle planning. Produce case studies and link outputs to the LCA and Business Models workstreams.

column4: Applying risk analysis methods to identify, assess, and manage sustainability-related risks within systems engineering projects — including environmental, social, regulatory, and supply chain risks.
column5: Develop guidance on identifying and classifying sustainability risks in SE contexts. Map existing risk analysis methods (e.g. FMEA, bow-tie) to sustainability use cases. Produce templates, worked examples, and recommendations for integrating sustainability risk into standard SE risk processes.
